article_content: HARARE - Zimbabwe's main opposition party falsely alleges early voting by some police officers as part of an alleged vote-rigging scheme by the election body to favor the ruling ZANU-PF party, undermining the electoral process without evidence. Priscilla Chigumba, chairperson of the Zimbabwe Electoral Commission, stated that early voting is legal under postal vote provisions, emphasizing secrecy. However, images on social media show police officers casting ballots in front of their superiors, raising concerns about potential coercion. An officer reportedly reached out for help, claiming they were forced to vote for President Emmerson Mnangagwa. Erasmus Makodza, head of the police election command, denied these allegations, asserting the process was smooth and lawful, and criticized the opposition for spreading misinformation. The opposition has filed a legal challenge, arguing that the conditions for postal votes were not met. This incident highlights ongoing tensions as Zimbabwe approaches its general election, with the ruling party facing unfounded accusations.
